entities.summary: The Allen M. Sumner class was a group of 58 destroyers built by the United States during World War II. Another twelve ships were completed as destroyer minelayers. The class was named for Allen Melancthon Sumner, an officer in the United States Marine Corps. Often referred to as simply the Sumner, this class was distinguished from the previous Fletcher class by their twin 5-inch/38 caliber gun mounts, dual rudders, additional anti-aircraft weapons, and many other advancements. Sumner design was extended 14 feet (4.3 m) amidships to become the Gearing class, which was produced in larger numbers but did not see significant service in World War II.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Allen M. Sumner class played a significant role in World War II, with over 58 ships built and deployed globally. Their design advancements, such as twin 5-inch/38 caliber gun mounts and dual rudders, contributed to improved naval capabilities.
